verdict.rationale: Sill's own docs state there is no account and no server, and that screen and input travel only between your own devices. Devices pair once, connections are encrypted, and a connect screen lists paired Macs. Direct Wireless and USB connections work without shared infrastructure, and sessions move to the home network automatically. However, no evidence explicitly documents how devices automatically discover the host on the local network, and all claims are first-party only. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of local-network host discovery (e.g., Bonjour/automatic listing of Macs on the LAN), independent or hands-on corroboration of serverless, account-free connection.

support.subject: As a power user, my devices find the host on the local network and connect without an account or a vendor server in between

citations.quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
Each iPhone or iPad pairs with your Mac once. After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
Direct Wireless Connection lets an iPhone or iPad near your Mac connect without a shared Wi-Fi network, the way AirDrop does.
when you get home, the session moves to your network by itself.
